curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Start with what pavement lines tell drivers, then broken versus solid lines, yellow versus white, reading the line on your left, the four-lane center, no passing zones and why the shoulder is never a passing lane.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per marking rule; contrast cards for broken versus solid, yellow versus white and the no passing zone versus a solid yellow line on your side.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz describing the lines beside a driver and asking whether passing is allowed.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Show where to stop at a stop line or crosswalk, who crosses there and when to yield, then dual-use arrows, the shared center lane against marked left-turn lanes, the never-back-up and never-stop rules, and lane choice on multi-lane roads.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per lane rule; contrast cards for the shared center lane versus a marked left-turn lane and backing up versus stopping in a travel lane.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz placing a driver in a lane or at a crosswalk and asking what to do.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Rank the traffic officer above every sign and signal, then teach steady red, right on red, steady yellow and green, the flashing red and flashing yellow look-alikes, when signals flash, and the dark signal treated as a four-way stop.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per signal meaning; contrast cards for flashing red versus steady red, flashing yellow versus steady yellow and a dark signal versus a flashing red.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz naming a light or an officer's signal and asking what the driver must do.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Separate the permissive, protected and protected and permissive left-turn phases, then walk through the steady red arrow, steady yellow arrow, flashing yellow arrow and green arrow with their look-alike pairs.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per phase or arrow; contrast cards for protected versus permissive, green arrow versus flashing yellow arrow and steady red arrow versus steady yellow arrow.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz naming an arrow or phase and asking whether the driver may turn and whom to yield to.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Teach the shape code from octagon to diamond, the rectangles and the railroad shapes, then the color code from red to brown, the yellow versus yellow green split, regulatory sign layouts and the red circle and slash.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per shape or color group; contrast cards for pennant versus pentagon and yellow versus yellow green.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz naming a shape or color and asking what kind of sign it marks.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Describe the yellow diamond warning sign, then the stop and signal ahead signs, school and pedestrian crossings, the added lane, merge and lane ends signs, and the intersection, side road, roundabout and side road railroad signs.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per warning sign; contrast cards for added lane versus merge, merge versus lane ends and intersection versus side road ahead.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz naming a warning sign and asking how the driver should respond.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Contrast turn, reverse turn and curve signs and their advised speeds, the advisory plate in bad weather, the exit ramp advisory, arrows and chevrons, then the slow-moving vehicle triangle, slick roads, soft shoulders, divided roadways, object markers and cyclists.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per sign; contrast cards for turn versus curve signs, the curve plate versus the exit ramp advisory and the orange vehicle triangle versus the yield triangle.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz describing a curve, a vehicle or a road condition sign and asking what it means.
